type: concept
title: "HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)"
---

## Summary

HNSW is a graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) index that organises
vectors into a multi-layer navigable small-world graph.

## Key Points

- Multi-layer graph with long-range links in upper layers.
- Greedy search from the top layer down gives logarithmic hops.

## Details

Construction inserts each point at a randomly chosen maximum layer and connects
it to its M nearest neighbours per layer; search descends layer by layer.

## Sources

- Malkov & Yashunin (2018), Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor
  search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs.

## Summary

HNSW is a graph-based approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) index.

## Key Points

- Multi-layer navigable small-world graph.
- Logarithmic expected search complexity.

## Details

Upper layers hold long-range links; lower layers are dense. Search is a greedy
descent from the entry point.

## Sources

- Malkov & Yashunin (2018), HNSW.
